 Mr. Debaraj Nayak, Advocate
 (for informant/victim)
 Coram:

Justice M.S.Sahoo
 Order
10.01.2025 Hybrid Mode Order No.

8. 1. Under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. the BLAPL has been filed by the petitioner in jail custody, in connection with Andhirakancha P.S. Case No.26 dated 10.04.2023 corresponding to T.R. Case No.10 of 2023 pending in the court of learned Addl. Sessions Judgecum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Rayagada for alleged commission of offences under Sections 376(2)(n)/376(3)/506/109/34 of IPC and Section 6 read with Section 5(I) /5(1) of POCSO Act, 2012.

2. Since the earlier BLAPL No.9098 of 2023 filed by the petitioner was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 07.12.2023 by this Bench, the present petition has been placed before this Bench for consideration of the renewed prayer for bail in terms of Standing Order No.2 of 2023 dated 21.05.2023.
3.
By order dated 8.04.2024 in terms of the provisions contained in Section 439(1-A), the informant/victim were noticed intimating their right of audience in the present proceeding.

Pursuant to the notice issued to the informant/victim they are represented by Mr. Nayak, learned legal aid defence counsel who is present at the virtual Court, High Court of Orissa, Rayagada and Jhintu Naik vs State Of Odisha & Another ....

entities.text: High Court of Orissa, Rayagada and Jhintu Naik vs State Of Odisha & Another
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opp. ...

on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33846597/
1 addresses arguments.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner reiterates the prayer of the petitioner to be granted bail as he is in custody since 11.04.2023 i.e. a period of incarceration for about 20 months.
5. The learned Additional Government Advocate referring to the materials contained in the case diary, status of trial, nature of allegations opposes the prayer for bail.
The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant/victim referring to the materials on record and the apprehension of the informant/victim opposes the prayer for bail.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Additional Government Advocate and the learned legal aid defence counsel for the informant/victim, in considered opinion of this Court the petitioner is not entitled for bail at this stage.
There is no further ground to revisit the order dated 07.12.2023 passed by this Court in BLAPL No.9098 of 2023 rejecting the prayer for bail.
The prayer for bail is rejected.

7. Pursuant to the orders of this Court dated 23.12.2024 the learned ADJ-cum-P.O., Special Court under POCSO Act, Rayagada has intimated the registry of this Court by her letter dated 07.01.2025 (which forms part of record) that further approximately four months should be necessary for completion of trial.

Out of 18 witnesses, 8 number of witnesses have been examined and the next date of posting is 07.01.2025.
8.

In the interest of justice it is directed that the trial of the case pending before the learned Special Court i.e. T.R. Case No.10 of 2023 arising out of Andhirakancha P.S. Case No.26 of 2023 dated 10.04.2023 shall be proceeded with expeditiously and be completed within five months.
The defence as well as prosecution are directed to make endeavour on each date for expeditious completion.
The registry shall communicate this order to the learned court in seisin of the matter.
(M.S. Sahoo) Judge RJ Jhintu Naik vs State Of Odisha & Another .... Opp. ... on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33846597/
